ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, D and E are points on sides AB and BC of $\triangle ABC$, respectively, and $DE\parallel AC$. AE and CD intersect at point O. If $\frac{S_{\triangle DOE}}{S_{\triangle COA}}=\frac{1}{25}$, what is the value of $\frac{S_{\triangle BDE}}{S_{\triangle CDE}}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $DE\parallel AC$,\\
$\therefore \triangle DEO\sim \triangle CAO$,\\
$\therefore \frac{{S}_{\triangle DEO}}{{S}_{\triangle CAO}}=\left(\frac{DE}{AC}\right)^{2}=\frac{1}{25}$,\\
$\therefore \frac{DE}{AC}=\frac{BE}{BC}=\frac{1}{5}$,\\
$\therefore \frac{BE}{EC}=\frac{1}{4}$,\\
$\therefore \frac{{S}_{\triangle BED}}{{S}_{\triangle DEC}}=\boxed{\frac{1}{4}}$.

If $\frac{S_{\triangle DOE}}{S_{\triangle COA}}=\frac{1}{25}$, what is the value of $\frac{S_{\triangle BDE}}{S_{\triangle CDE}}$?
ready3_open_rewrite.raw_answer: Given that $DE\parallel AC$, $\triangle DEO\sim \triangle CAO$, so $\frac{S_{\triangle DEO}}{S_{\triangle CAO}}=\left(\frac{DE}{AC}\right)^2=\frac{1}{25}$. Therefore $\frac{DE}{AC}=\frac{BE}{BC}=\frac{1}{5}$, hence $\frac{BE}{EC}=\frac{1}{4}$, and $\frac{S_{\triangle BED}}{S_{\triangle DEC}}=\frac{1}{4}$.

Image description: In the figure is triangle ABC, B and C are on the base BC, and A is at the upper right; D is located on side AB, and E is located on side BC; the short line segment DE is parallel to the right side AC; line segments AE and CD intersect at point O in the interior.

Reasoning: Because DE ∥ AC, and O is at the intersection point of AE and CD, ∠DOE and ∠COA are vertical angles, and there are also corresponding angles obtained from parallel lines being equal, therefore △DOE ∼ △COA. The ratio of the areas of similar triangles is equal to the square of the ratio of corresponding side lengths, so S△DOE / S△COA = (DE/AC)^2 = 1/25, therefore DE/AC = 1/5. Also because DE ∥ AC, △BDE ∼ △BAC, so BE/BC = DE/AC = 1/5. Thus EC/BC = 4/5, hence BE/EC = 1/4. Finally, the bases BE and CE of △BDE and △CDE are both on the line BC, and their heights from D to BC are the same, so the area ratio is equal to the base ratio: S△BDE / S△CDE = BE/CE = 1/4.
